reuse.why: Most bulk actions share category selection and existing budget primitives, but copyPreviousMonth bypasses that selection and setBulkNMonthAvg reproduces setNMonthAvg's calculation-and-write logic.

duplication.why: Hidden-category filtering and saved-template exclusion each have separate SQL and JavaScript implementations, while bulk and single-category averaging duplicate calculation, sign adjustment, and writing.

placement.why: Category eligibility and budget calculations remain in the budget actions module, with handler registration and undo integration in the existing application layer.

scope.why: The edits are confined to the requested month-wide budget actions, their registration, and related tests.

maintainability.why: The shared bulk helpers improve ownership, but parallel eligibility implementations and duplicated averaging logic require coordinated changes across multiple paths.

bypasses_abstraction.where: packages/loot-core/src/server/budget/actions.ts: copyPreviousMonth implements eligibility outside getBulkBudgetCategories/shouldSkipBulkCategory, and setBulkNMonthAvg reproduces work already encapsulated by setNMonthAvg.

disguised_duplication.where: packages/loot-core/src/server/budget/actions.ts: SQL eligibility predicates are restated as JavaScript checks in copyPreviousMonth, and setBulkNMonthAvg reshapes setNMonthAvg's averaging, sign adjustment, and budget write.

abstraction_drift.where: packages/loot-core/src/server/budget/actions.ts: includeHiddenCategories introduces one policy option, while copyPreviousMonth retains separate eligibility logic and setBulkNMonthAvg bypasses the existing single-category averaging action.
